basis: All five absence claims re-derived independently at 06d9f8ce. (1) `git ls-tree --name-only <rev> internal/platform/` returns canonjson, cardutil, config, crypto, resilience, storage, telemetry — no cache/, no errors/. Three documents assert both: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:85 `cache/` and :89 `errors/` inside its platform block, internal/README.md:52/:56 (tree box) and :240/:243 (package table), and CLAUDE.md:38's platform bullet ('cache, config, crypto, resilience, telemetry'). (2) `git grep -rn 'NewCardSliceCache' <rev>` returns exactly one line, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:155, inside the '## Cache System' section that opens at :134 — no Go source. (3) docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:200 '### TCGdex.dev' and :204 'Code: internal/adapters/clients/tcgdex/'; `git ls-tree --name-only <rev> internal/adapters/clients/` returns cardladder dh dhlisting dhprice google httpx psa psaportal — no tcgdex. `git grep -in tcgdex <rev> -- internal cmd web` hits only internal/testutil/mocks/http_client.go:30,119,120,125 (doc-comment example URLs) and http_client_test.go:162. (4) docs/SCHEDULERS.md:106 '### Cache Warmup', :108 '**File:** cache_warmup.go', :115-117 the three env gates, repeated at :207 in the file-layout block. `git grep -n CACHE_WARMUP <rev> -- internal cmd .env.example` is empty; `git ls-tree --name-only <rev> internal/adapters/scheduler/` contains no cache_warmup.go. (5) docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:285 asserts .github/workflows/fly-deploy.yml with FLY_API_TOKEN; `git ls-tree --name-only <rev> .github/workflows/` returns browser-matrix, dependabot-auto-merge, docker-build, frontend-ci, psa-harvest-cron, test — no fly-deploy.yml. Every command executes and its output matches. All five hold; severity high is carried by the operational half (a phantom deploy pipeline in the ops doc, and three phantom env gates an operator could try to set).
what_the_finding_got_wrong: One parenthetical sub-claim inside evidence leg 1 is false: 'canonjson/ and cardutil/ exist and appear in no document.' cardutil/ IS documented — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:86 ('cardutil/  # Card name/set normalization') and internal/README.md:53. Only canonjson/ is undocumented. The leg's load-bearing claim (cache/ and errors/ are documented and absent) is unaffected. Separately, internal/platform/storage/ exists in the tree and is missing from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's platform list — an additional instance of the same defect the finding did not claim, so the fix scope in acceptance criterion 2 is slightly larger than the evidence enumerates.

basis: Re-derived each path claim, and cleared the same-name-collision trap first. `git ls-tree --name-only <rev> internal/domain/inventory/` contains core_types.go and no types.go and no types_core.go; the two doc citations are fully directory-qualified ('internal/domain/inventory/types.go' at docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:34, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:52 inside the `inventory/` block of the package tree), so neither can be pointing at a different same-named file. internal/README.md:627's `domain/inventory/types_core.go | 562 | Core domain types: Campaign, Purchase, Sale, Phase, DH status` is provably the same file: core_types.go is 562 lines (`git show <rev>:internal/domain/inventory/core_types.go | grep -c ''` → 562). service_interfaces.go: `git grep -nE 'type [A-Za-z]+Repository interface' <rev> -- internal/domain/inventory/service_interfaces.go` is empty (exit 1); `git grep -nE 'type [A-Za-z]+ interface'` on the same file returns exactly six service interfaces (AnalyticsService, CertService, PricingService, DHService, CertLookupService, SnapshotService) at :14,:33,:42,:59,:66,:72 — so docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:240-244's five repository rows and :53's 'ObjFocused repository interfaces' comment and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:34 all point at the wrong contract. pricelookup: no tracked path matches (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> | grep -i pricelookup` empty); the real package is internal/domain/pricing/lookup, and the wrong citation appears three times (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:40, :58, :224). dh_helpers.go resolves only to internal/domain/dhlisting/, not inventory/ (docs/DH_INVENTORY.md:198). docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:23-24's two 'Price Units (Critical)' key files match no tracked path. CLAUDE.md:85's `ls internal/domain/inventory/parse_*.go` matches nothing (only confidence_parse_test.go, which does not match the prefix), and internal/domain/csvimport/service.go's header states it was carved out of inventory under SLA-35 while internal/README.md:86 still attributes 'CSV import' to inventory/ and omits csvimport from the table.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The title is inaccurate: core_types.go is given TWO wrong names (types.go, types_core.go) across THREE documents, not 'four different wrong names across four documents'. The finding's own evidence leg 1 states the correct two-name/three-document picture, so this is a title defect only. Two line-number drifts: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's `types.go` is at :52 and `service_interfaces.go` at :53, not the :50/:51 the finding cites (the :240-244 table range is exact); CLAUDE.md's parse_*.go locator is at :85, not :84. Also unclaimed but in the same fix scope: the pricelookup mislocation recurs at docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:58 and :224, not only :40.

basis: Both halves hold, and I established both statically without executing either monitoring command or touching a database or server. Half 1: I enumerated the registered surface myself from `git show <rev>:internal/adapters/httpserver/routes.go` and `:router.go` rather than trusting the docs-map. router.go registers only /api/auth/logout (:235), /api/auth/user (:236), /api/health (:246); routes.go registers 127 path literals. Cross-checking README.md:88-113's nineteen rows: /api/campaigns/{id}/archive, /api/campaigns/{id}/purchases/import, /api/campaigns/cash-flow, /api/sets, /api/cards/search, /api/favorites and /api/status/api-usage appear in neither file. `git grep -rn 'archive|cash-flow|"favorites"' <rev> -- internal/adapters/httpserver/` (non-test) is empty, ruling out prefix-mux dispatch inside a handler; the registered campaign subpaths are the 24 explicit literals at routes.go:107-145 with no archive and no cash-flow, the real import routes are /api/purchases/import-{certs,external,orders,psa} (routes.go:148-154), and the real usage route is /api/admin/api-usage (routes.go:43). Half 2: `git grep -n 'cache-stats' <rev>` returns exactly one line tree-wide — docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:235 itself. cmd/slabledger/admin.go:15-25 is a closed switch over 'version', 'print-config', 'help/--help/-h' with a default returning `unknown admin command: %s`, so `./slabledger admin cache-stats` provably errors without being run. The second command's target, /api/status/api-usage, is unregistered per half 1, so it provably 404s.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The count is off by one, in the direction that understates the defect: the finding's title and evidence say 'six of the nineteen', then enumerate seven paths. The enumerated list is complete and correct; the word 'six' (and the docs-map note's 'remaining thirteen', really twelve) is wrong. This miscount originates in the docs-map record README.md:endpoint-table-unregistered-routes and was copied forward. Second, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's Monitoring section (:228) contains THREE commands, not two — `curl /api/health` is registered at router.go:246 and works. The finding's 'both of DEVELOPMENT.md's monitoring commands fail' is true of the two it names but is not true of the section. Acceptance criterion 2 ('Both commands ... execute successfully against a running local server') is therefore mis-scoped and cannot be satisfied as written for a doc-only fix; a fixer should restate it as 'each command in the Monitoring section names a registered route or an implemented subcommand'.

basis: All four legs re-derived by reading the referenced symbols at 06d9f8ce and comparing signatures; I did not modify any file to build. (1) `git grep -nE 'ErrDuplicateCert\b' <rev> -- '*.go'` is empty (exit 1) — the \b anchor correctly excludes ErrDuplicateCertNumber, which is the real symbol, declared at internal/domain/inventory/errors.go:33 and used at nine Go sites. The unqualified `git grep -nE 'ErrDuplicateCert' <rev>` shows internal/testutil/mocks/README.md:176 as the only occurrence of the bare name anywhere. Copying that identifier into a test is an undefined-symbol compile error. (2) `git grep -n GetPriceFunc <rev>` returns internal/README.md:271 and :275 only — no Go source. The real type at internal/testutil/mocks/price_provider.go:11-14 is `struct { behavior MockBehavior; matches map[string]*pricing.Price }`, both unexported, configured via NewMockPriceProvider(opts ...MockOption) at :16. The README's `package mocks` example redeclares MockPriceProvider with a public GetPriceFunc field, so pasted into that package it is both a redeclaration error and a description of a type that does not exist. (3) internal/testutil/mocks/README.md:15 reads 'All mocks use the **Fn-field pattern**: every interface method has a corresponding `Fn` field.' MockPriceProvider has no Fn field, so the universal is false within the same package the README documents. (4) `git grep -n 'package picks|package favorites' <rev>` returns only internal/testutil/mocks/README.md:182, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> | grep -iE 'picks|favorites'` is entirely empty — neither package, nor any file whose name contains either word, exists in the tree. The carve-out is for two nonexistent packages.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Leg 3 is the weakest and is loosely described. The README does not 'concede the exception' at :184 — that line says `MockBehavior`/`MockOption` in common.go 'are used only by card/HTTP mocks (legacy); prefer the Fn-field pattern for all new mocks', which implies a legacy exception without naming MockPriceProvider. The contradiction with the :15 universal is real but softer than 'the headline rule and the caveat contradict each other'. The arithmetic is also wrong: :184 is 169 lines after :15, not 176, and the file is 185 lines total. Second, a subject-scope mismatch: the finding's subject identity is internal/testutil/mocks/README.md, but leg 2 (the only 'worked example' leg, and the one carrying the compile claim in the title) lives in internal/README.md:271. A fixer working from the subject line alone would edit the wrong file for a quarter of the finding; the finding's own prose does say so, but acceptance criterion 2 ('the example code block compiles when pasted into a scratch test in internal/testutil/mocks/') does not name which file's example it means.

basis:
Judged as a lead, per the controller's instruction. Both citations are accurate at 06d9f8ce and both paths are genuinely unregistered. internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/api_status_handler.go:30 reads `// apiUsageResponse is the JSON response for GET /api/status/api-usage.` internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/spa_handler.go:133 emits `
  • /api/sets - List available sets
    • ` into the fallback HTML page. Neither /api/status/api-usage nor /api/sets appears in routes.go's 127 registered path literals or router.go's three; `git grep -nE '"/api/(sets|favorites|cards/search|campaigns/cash-flow)' -- internal cmd` returns only spa_handler.go:133 and middleware/security_headers_test.go:188. The lead is sound and correctly routed out of the docs lane for the spa_handler half.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The dead-code framing is wrong for the first of the two items. The pointer asks 'whether the handler behind the first is reachable at all' — but that handler IS registered and live: routes.go:43 wires rt.apiStatusHandler.HandleAPIUsage behind /api/admin/api-usage under RequireAdmin. So there is no reachability question there at all, only a stale path string in a doc-comment on the apiUsageResponse type (which is itself live, being the marshalled response). Only the spa_handler.go:133 half is a genuine reachability lead, and even that is one step removed: the question is whether the fallback HTML page is ever served, not whether the symbol is referenced. dead-code-go should be told the first half is a comment fix, not a reachability investigation, or it will spend a pass proving a live handler live. Not ticketable on its own by construction — it is a pointer whose acceptance criterion is that the owning lens absorbs it.

basis: Both halves are factually true. Half A: internal/README.md:138 reads '`advisor → ai`, `advisor → scoring`, `dhlisting → dhevents`, `pricing/lookup → pricing`,' continuing at :139 with '`inventory → dhevents`, `inventory → intelligence`.' — the entire worked example for the leaf rule. `git ls-tree -d --name-only <rev> internal/domain/advisor internal/domain/ai internal/domain/scoring` is empty: none of the three is a tracked tree, so three of the six example edges dangle at both ends of two of them. `git rev-parse <rev>^` is e46370e531a57538c40a5d75993ccb2ed1277422, and `git show e46370e5 --stat -- internal/README.md` shows that commit did open this file (2 deletions, removing the other scoring/ mentions) while leaving :138 untouched — the staleness is exactly one commit old and was introduced by a sweep with the file open. Half B: running CLAUDE.md's own derivation command at the baseline yields eleven packages (arbitrage, csvimport, demand, dhlisting, dhpricing, export, finance, portfolio, pricing/lookup, psacampaign, tuning); CLAUDE.md:116-118 lists ten, omitting csvimport. The finding is right that this is not an enforcement gap — scripts/check-imports.sh derives membership from the tree.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Nothing factual. The severity is overstated at medium once the two halves are weighed separately. Half B is a self-acknowledged defect: CLAUDE.md:106-118 states the roster is derived not listed, supplies the exact derivation command three lines above the list, and closes the sentence with 'but derive it rather than trusting this sentence.' A reader following the document as written never relies on the stale list, and the finding itself concedes there is no enforcement consequence — so half B is close to zero-impact and cannot carry a medium. Half A is a genuine defect with no disclaimer, but its consequence is comprehension friction in one illustrative paragraph: the rule itself, its enforcement, and the three surviving legal edges are all still correct, and the reader can substitute any live leaf. That is a low. Ticketability is unaffected — the four acceptance criteria are the sharpest in this batch and a fixer can prove the fix from them alone.
